title: Three-Scenario Priority Slate and Exec Asks (Q3 planning) v0.1
content:
Purpose: quick, shareable working slate to align exec asks and top-level OKR candidates across three plausible company scenarios for the upcoming quarter. Treat as a synthesis: not final, intended for exec review ahead of the all-hands planning session.

High-level framing / why this format:
- Problem: too many competing asks across GTM, Eng, Product; need a clear mapping from external signals (demand, capacity, macro) to a small set of prioritized outcomes.
- Approach: propose 3 scenarios (Grow, Protect, Optimize) with 2–3 top bets per scenario. For each bet: proposed OKR phrasing (candidate), rough success metric, primary owner, and an explicit "exec ask" (funding/headcount/rollback authority).
- Outcome desired: by end of exec sync (Mar week 2) we have 1) chosen scenario prioritization, 2) committed exec asks (who signs), 3) a short runbook for the all-hands launch and comms.

Scenario A — Grow (aggressive market capture)
- Context: cloud demand continues to expand, competitors slow to ship regional capacity; opportunity to push hosted API adoption and PLG motion.
- Top bets (2):
  1) Hosted API performance sprint (reduce median generation latency by 20% for standard models)
     - Candidate OKR: "Improve hosted API median latency by 20% on our core text-gen models (p50)"
     - Measure: p50 latency for text-gen endpoints (global), measured in console dashboards; target baseline = 180ms -> goal 144ms.
     - Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Samir)
     - Exec ask: +2 infra SWE contractors for 8 weeks; immediate priority on kernel selection and scheduler tuning.
  2) PLG conversion push (product-led onboarding funnel optimization)
     - Candidate OKR: "Increase free->paid conversion rate by 30% for developer signups"
     - Measure: cohort conversion within 14 days, tracked in Growth GA and internal funnel dashboard.
     - Owner: growth/product (Priya)
     - Exec ask: reallocate one growth PM and $60k in developer credit incentives for experiment budget.
- Risks & mitigations: risk of engineering burnout; mitigation = explicit non-go plan for lower-priority initiatives and hiring contractors.

Scenario B — Protect (SLA & enterprise focus)
- Context: a small set of enterprise prospects are in security/finance and need Private/Dedicated SLAs. Focus on reducing variance and compliance work.
- Top bets (2):
  1) Private deployment hardened checklist + audit readiness
     - Candidate OKR: "Deliver private deployment baseline (VPC) with SOC-type audit artifacts for first 3 customers"
     - Measure: internal SOC readiness checklist completed + two external trial signups.
     - Owner: private-deployments (Evelyn)
     - Exec ask: 1 technical program manager + $40k in third-party audit support (preparation).
  2) Dedicated capacity SLO stabilization
     - Candidate OKR: "Achieve 99.9% uptime for Dedicated clusters and reduce p95 latency variance by 30%"
     - Measure: uptime / latency variance in Redwood Console per-cluster.
     - Owner: dedicated (Miguel)
     - Exec ask: freeze non-critical feature launches for 6 weeks, and reassign 2 SREs to Dedicated onboarding.
- Risks & mitigations: slows PLG momentum; mitigation = time-boxed focus and customer contract incentives to justify the trade.

Scenario C — Optimize (unit economics & reliability)
- Context: macro enters cautious mode; top priority is reducing per-token costs and improving predictability for customers.
- Top bets (3):
  1) Quantization & model-selection playbook for cost-sensitive workloads
     - Candidate OKR: "Reduce average per-token serving cost by 18% for top 10 customers"
     - Measure: per-customer cost curves in billing pipeline.
     - Owner: applied-ml (Samir + Jorge)
     - Exec ask: support from infra to test quantized variants in staging (2 GPUs for 4 weeks).
  2) Caching & batching default config rollout
     - Candidate OKR: "Increase platform-wide effective throughput via caching/batching to cut per-token latency-adjusted cost by 12%"
     - Measure: token-level cost delta, adoption of new defaults in Console.
     - Owner: serving-runtime (Samir)
     - Exec ask: temporary product change window to flip defaults + comms to customers.
  3) Cost transparency & customer cost-savings toolkit
     - Candidate OKR: "Ship customer-facing cost insights dashboard and automated optimization suggestions"
     - Measure: dashboard adoption and 5 pilot customers implementing suggestions.
     - Owner: console-and-tooling (Priya)
     - Exec ask: 1 FE engineer + UX contractor for 6 weeks.
- Risks & mitigations: may feel incremental; mitigation = package wins as savings guarantee offers for select customers.

Cross-scenario constraints and assumptions (shared):
- Hiring runway: we assume ability to convert two existing contractors to full-time within quarter (confirm with People).
- Budget sensitivity: scenario Grow needs short-term spend; Protect requires reallocation; Optimize is lowest immediate spend but needs engineering cycles.
- Key metric dependencies: latency telemetry, cost per token pipeline, and conversion funnel must be green (links in linked_artifacts).

Proposed OKR shortlist (flattened for prioritization grid)
- O1: Improve hosted API median latency by 20% (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- O2: Increase free->paid conversion by 30% (owner: growth/product)
- O3: Deliver private deployment audit artifacts for 3 customers (owner: private-deployments)
- O4: Achieve 99.9% uptime for Dedicated clusters (owner: dedicated)
- O5: Reduce per-token serving cost by 18% for top customers (owner: applied-ml)
- O6: Ship cost insights dashboard (owner: console-and-tooling)

Decision ask for execs (what we need from you)
- 1) Scenario selection: pick one scenario to be the "company priority" for the quarter and designate 1 exec sponsor. Decision needed by Mar 10.
- 2) Budget approvals: pre-approve the exec asks listed above for immediate ramp (detailed numbers in linked_confluence page).
- 3) Hiring flex: sign-off to reallocate 2 SRE / infra FTEs temporarily if Protect or Grow chosen.
- 4) All-hands signal: approve the 10-minute exec opening script concept and a 60-second CEO ask (draft below).

All-hands planning quick notes (ops & comms)
- Proposed cadence: executive opening (10m) -> scenario + chosen bets (10m) -> team breakouts (30m) -> synthesis and commitment board (10m).
- Messages to land: clarity on tradeoffs (why we picked this scenario), what success looks like (metrics), and where teams can find the short runbooks.
- Pre-reads: 1-pager scenario deck (2 slides), detailed OKR candidate sheet (spreadsheet link), FAQ for managers. Send 4 days prior.
- Post-all-hands: commit board exported to Jira (auto-create PLAN tickets). Owner: company-ops (Asha).

Risks & open questions (notes-to-self / items to resolve)
- Q: do we have telemetry parity across regions to measure p50 reliably? (Action: SRE to confirm; Jira: INF-442)
- Q: legal review time for Private audit materials — how long? (Action: Legal / Security to estimate.)
- Blocker: growth infra experiment platform stability for free->paid cohort tracking. (Action: Growth eng to triage.)

Next steps (immediate)
- Today: share this doc with execs + link to scenario slide (Asha).
- By Mar 3: execs indicate preferred scenario in Slack thread (linked_artifacts).
- By Mar 10: formal decision + approve budget ask numbers.
- Mar week 2: all-hands execution and roll to teams.

Appendix (short):
- Quick comms draft for CEO (60s): "This quarter we pick one clear path so each team can lock in. We will focus on [SCENARIO_NAME] — this means X hires and Y spend. Our top metric is Z. I ask each manager to align team OKRs this week and bring a short plan to the breakout."
- Quick exec script (10m): 2m context; 4m scenario explanation and ask; 2m Q&A; 2m commit call-to-action.

Labels: working-draft; expect multiple iterations. Comments welcome inline or in the planning thread.

-- Asha
